title: Ileocolic Intussusception
description: Confirm with ultrasound, reduce by enema without routine antibiotics, retry a partial reduction when the child is stable, discharge after observation, and operate laparoscopically when enemas fail.
objectives: Reduce by enema with surgical backup and without prophylactic antibiotics
Select children for a delayed repeat enema after partial reduction
Discharge from the emergency department after about 4 hours of observation
Use a laparoscopic approach when enema reduction fails

references.citation: Kelley-Quon LI, Arthur LG, Williams RF, et al. Management of intussusception in children: A systematic review. J Pediatr Surg. 2021;56(3):587-596.

Tsou PY, Wang YH, Ma YK, et al. Accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound and radiology-performed ultrasound for intussusception: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Am J Emerg Med. 2019;37(9):1760-1769.
Raval MV, Minneci PC, Deans KJ, et al. Improving Quality and Efficiency for Intussusception Management After Successful Enema Reduction. Pediatrics. 2015;136(5):e1345-e1352.

start.text: A 14-month-old boy has had episodes of inconsolable crying with drawing up of the legs for 12 hours, between which he is quiet. He has vomited twice. There is a vague mass in the right upper abdomen. He is alert and well perfused, with no peritonitis.

options.label: Abdominal ultrasound
options.feedback: In a meta-analysis of 30 studies (5,249 children), ultrasound had 98% sensitivity and 98% specificity for intussusception. Point-of-care ultrasound by emergency physicians performed as well as radiology-performed scans.

options.label: CT of the abdomen
options.feedback: Ultrasound is the diagnostic test: 98% sensitive and 98% specific across 30 studies, whether performed by radiologists or emergency physicians (Tsou 2019).

reduce.text: Ultrasound shows an ileocolic intussusception. How do you set up the reduction?

options.label: Enema reduction with a clinician able to decompress a pneumoperitoneum present, and surgeons available; no prophylactic antibiotics
options.feedback: APSA 2021: prophylactic antibiotics before enema reduction do not reduce complications and are unnecessary (grade C). A physician able to decompress a pneumoperitoneum and perform resuscitation should be present, and emergency pediatric surgery should be available in the hospital system (grade D).

options.label: IV antibiotics first, then enema reduction
options.feedback: APSA 2021 (grade C): prophylactic antibiotics before enema reduction do not decrease post-reduction complications and are unnecessary in stable children without critical illness.

options.label: Laparotomy without attempting an enema
options.feedback: APSA 2021: in hemodynamically stable children without critical illness, non-operative management should be maximized. Across studies, 76.8% of enema reductions succeeded.

reduced.text: The enema reduces the intussusception fully. He is well, and his family lives 15 minutes away. Plan?

options.label: Observe in the emergency department for about 4 hours, then discharge with return advice
options.feedback: APSA 2021: complication rates do not differ between emergency department observation and admission, so children may be discharged from the ED. About 4 hours of observation appears optimal (grade C). Teach parents the symptoms of recurrence, check they can return, and warn that recurrence is slightly more likely over age 2. In Raval 2015's discharge pathway, 30 of 46 eligible children went home from the ED, and one returned needing a repeat enema.

options.label: Admit for 48 hours of observation
options.feedback: APSA 2021: there is no evidence of more complications after ED observation than after admission; after about 4 hours of observation, children can be discharged with return advice when the family can get back easily.

partial.text: The enema moves the intussusceptum but does not reduce it fully. He remains stable with no peritonitis. Next?

options.label: Straight to theatre
options.feedback: APSA 2021 (grade C): a delayed repeat enema is reasonable for a stable child without peritonitis whose first enema achieved partial reduction. It raises overall success by almost 10%, and about half of first-enema failures avoid surgery, with similar perforation and resection rates.

options.label: Delayed repeat enema after 30 minutes to 4 hours
options.feedback: APSA 2021: a stable child without peritonitis whose first enema achieved partial reduction can have a delayed repeat enema (grade C). Waiting 30 minutes to 4 hours between attempts is likely safe (grade D). Delayed enemas succeeded in 57.2% of attempts, with perforation similar to first enemas (1.1% of attempts).

failed.text: Repeated enemas fail. He is stable. Operative approach?

options.label: Initial laparoscopic approach, with open conversion if needed
options.feedback: APSA 2021 (grade C): no approach is proven superior for recurrence or complications, but an initial laparoscopic approach should be considered for its shorter stay and equivalent complication rates. A simultaneous air or saline enema may help laparoscopic reduction.

options.label: Midline laparotomy as the standard
options.feedback: APSA 2021 (grade C): consider an initial laparoscopic approach. It shortens stay with complication rates equivalent to open surgery.

appendix.text: Laparoscopic reduction succeeds. The bowel is viable, and the appendix looks normal. Remove the appendix?

options.label: No: incidental appendectomy does not reduce recurrence
options.feedback: APSA 2021 (grade D): data do not support prophylactic appendectomy during surgery for intussusception, as it does not seem to reduce recurrence. Consider removal only if the appendix is inflamed or ischemic.

options.label: Yes: always remove it to prevent recurrence
options.feedback: APSA 2021 (grade D): appendectomy does not seem to reduce recurrent intussusception. Removal can be considered only when the appendix is inflamed or ischemic.

fail_imaging.text: Guideline Deviation: CT instead of the diagnostic ultrasound.

fail_surgery.text: Guideline Deviation: Avoidable or more invasive surgery.

fail_admit.text: Guideline Deviation: Admission without a clinical reason.

success.text: Case Complete: Intussusception reduced with the least invasive effective step.
